content_voiceover: The fifth edition WHO classification refines CMML diagnosis in several testable ways. First, the absolute monocytosis threshold was lowered, persistent monocytosis of at least five hundred per microliter, together with monocytes making up at least ten percent of the white count, now satisfies the prerequisite criterion, a lower bar than before. Second, flow cytometry showing abnormal partitioning of peripheral blood monocyte subsets is now a recognized supporting criterion, with a characteristic increase in classical monocytes above a ninety four percent cutoff serving as a reproducible, objective marker in CMML. Third, subtyping still splits into myelodysplastic CMML, with a white count under thirteen, and myeloproliferative CMML, at or above thirteen, and the proliferative subtype is notably enriched for activating RAS pathway mutations along with worse clinical outcomes. Finally, note that the CMML-zero category, which existed under the blast and promonocyte based grading in earlier schemes, has been eliminated in this edition, leaving CMML-1 and CMML-2 as the only subgrouping tiers.
keypoints: Absolute monocytosis threshold lowered to 500/uL for CMML prerequisite criteria
Classical monocyte fraction over 94% by flow supports CMML diagnosis
MP-CMML (WBC 13 or higher) enriched for RAS pathway mutations, worse outcomes
CMML-0 category no longer exists; only CMML-1 and CMML-2 remain
keypoint_voiceover: High yield changes in the fifth edition CMML criteria, the monocytosis cutoff dropped to five hundred per microliter, monocyte subset flow cytometry with a classical monocyte cutoff above ninety four percent is now a supporting criterion, myeloproliferative CMML links to RAS pathway mutations and worse prognosis, and the CMML-zero grade has been retired, leaving just CMML-1 and CMML-2.
